lung.label: Right lung, 3 lobes
lung.title: Right lung
lung.body: Three lobes: upper, middle and lower, split by the horizontal and oblique fissures.

lung.label: Left lung, 2 lobes
lung.title: Left lung
lung.body: Two lobes and a lingula. The cardiac notch leaves room for the heart.

lung.label: Type II cell
lung.title: Type II cell
lung.body: Makes surfactant and repairs the alveolar lining.

lung.label: Alveolar wall
lung.title: Alveolar epithelium
lung.body: A thin lining of type I cells. Gas crosses it and the capillary wall in a fraction of a micron.

heart.label: Right ventricle
heart.title: Right ventricle
heart.body: Thin-walled and low pressure. It sits at the front of the heart.

heart.label: Left ventricle
heart.title: Left ventricle
heart.body: Thick-walled, high pressure pump that forms the apex.

heart.label: Cardiomyocyte
heart.title: Cardiomyocyte
heart.body: Striated muscle cell packed with mitochondria.

heart.label: Beta receptor
heart.title: Beta receptor
heart.body: Where adrenaline and dobutamine raise rate and force.

kidney.label: Cortex
kidney.title: Renal cortex
kidney.body: The outer layer. It holds the glomeruli and the proximal tubules, the most oxygen-hungry part.

kidney.label: Renal pelvis
kidney.title: Renal pelvis
kidney.body: Collects urine from the calyces and drains to the ureter.

kidney.label: Proximal tubule
kidney.title: Proximal tubule
kidney.body: Reabsorbs most of the filtered sodium, water, glucose and bicarbonate.

kidney.label: Tubular cell
kidney.title: Tubular cell
kidney.body: Brush border on the lumen side and mitochondria packed at the base.

liver.label: Right lobe
liver.title: Right lobe
liver.body: The larger lobe. It receives portal blood from the gut.

liver.label: Left lobe
liver.title: Left lobe
liver.body: The smaller lobe, in front of the stomach.

liver.label: Hepatocyte
liver.title: Hepatocyte
liver.body: Makes glucose, clotting factors, albumin and bile.

liver.label: Sinusoid
liver.title: Sinusoid
liver.body: The leaky capillary that bathes hepatocytes in portal and arterial blood.

brain.label: Cerebellum
brain.title: Cerebellum
brain.body: Sits in the posterior fossa. Swelling here can block CSF flow.

brain.label: Neurone
brain.title: Neuron
brain.body: The cell that fires. It is the first to fail when oxygen or glucose is short.

brain.label: Astrocyte foot
brain.title: Astrocyte end-foot
brain.body: Wraps the capillary and helps form the blood-brain barrier.

pancreas.label: Acinar cell
pancreas.title: Acinar cell
pancreas.body: Makes digestive enzymes and packs them in zymogen granules.

pancreas.label: Zymogen granule
pancreas.title: Zymogen granule
pancreas.body: Stores inactive enzymes. They should only activate in the gut.

bowel.label: Villus
bowel.title: Villus
bowel.body: Finger-like fold that absorbs nutrients. Its tip is the first to suffer low flow.

bowel.label: Enterocyte
bowel.title: Enterocyte
bowel.body: The absorbing cell, joined to its neighbours by tight junctions.

muscle.label: Muscle fibre
muscle.title: Muscle fibre
muscle.body: A long cell full of contractile proteins and myoglobin.

muscle.label: Sarcolemma
muscle.title: Sarcolemma
muscle.body: The cell membrane. When it fails, potassium, CK and myoglobin leak out.

skin.label: Dermal vessel
skin.title: Dermal vessel
skin.body: Small vessel in the dermis that feeds the skin.

vessel.label: Endothelium
vessel.title: Endothelium
vessel.body: The inner lining of the vessel. It controls tone, permeability and clotting.

bleed.label: Platelet
bleed.title: Platelet
bleed.body: Seals a gap in the vessel wall, then supports the fibrin clot.

ards.label: Dependent consolidation
ards.title: Dependent consolidation
ards.body: Fluid-filled and collapsed alveoli sit in the dependent (posterior) lung. Proning moves the load and recruits them.
ards.care: Helps: Lung-protective ventilation (about 6 ml/kg predicted weight, plateau below 30), prone positioning, conservative fluids. Avoid: Large tidal volume, high driving pressure, fluid overload.

ards.label: Patchy ground glass
ards.title: Patchy ground glass
ards.body: Inflamed but still aerated lung at the front. This is the small 'baby lung' that large breaths can overdistend.
ards.care: Helps: Lung-protective ventilation (about 6 ml/kg predicted weight, plateau below 30), prone positioning, conservative fluids. Avoid: Large tidal volume, high driving pressure, fluid overload.

ards.label: Wet, heavy lung
ards.title: Wet, heavy lung
ards.body: The cut face is red, wet and heavy with protein-rich oedema and blood. Lungs can weigh two to three times normal.
ards.care: Helps: Lung-protective ventilation (about 6 ml/kg predicted weight, plateau below 30), prone positioning, conservative fluids. Avoid: Large tidal volume, high driving pressure, fluid overload.

ards.label: Hyaline membrane
ards.title: Hyaline membrane
ards.body: A pink film of plasma protein and dead cell debris lining the alveolus. It blocks gas exchange.
ards.care: Helps: Lung-protective ventilation (about 6 ml/kg predicted weight, plateau below 30), prone positioning, conservative fluids. Avoid: Large tidal volume, high driving pressure, fluid overload.

ards.label: Alveolar oedema
ards.title: Oedema fluid
ards.body: Leaky capillaries and a damaged epithelium let protein-rich fluid flood the air space.
ards.care: Helps: Lung-protective ventilation (about 6 ml/kg predicted weight, plateau below 30), prone positioning, conservative fluids. Avoid: Large tidal volume, high driving pressure, fluid overload.

pancreatitis-ards.label: Dependent consolidation
pancreatitis-ards.title: Dependent consolidation
pancreatitis-ards.body: Fluid-filled and collapsed alveoli sit in the dependent (posterior) lung. Proning moves the load and recruits them.
pancreatitis-ards.care: Helps: Lung-protective ventilation (about 6 ml/kg predicted weight, plateau below 30), prone positioning, conservative fluids. Avoid: Large tidal volume, high driving pressure, fluid overload. Also treat the pancreatitis: early enteral feeding, no routine antibiotics unless infected necrosis.

pancreatitis-ards.label: Patchy ground glass
pancreatitis-ards.title: Patchy ground glass
pancreatitis-ards.body: Inflamed but still aerated lung at the front. This is the small 'baby lung' that large breaths can overdistend.
pancreatitis-ards.care: Helps: Lung-protective ventilation (about 6 ml/kg predicted weight, plateau below 30), prone positioning, conservative fluids. Avoid: Large tidal volume, high driving pressure, fluid overload.

pancreatitis-ards.label: Wet, heavy lung
pancreatitis-ards.title: Wet, heavy lung
pancreatitis-ards.body: The cut face is red, wet and heavy with protein-rich oedema and blood. Lungs can weigh two to three times normal.
pancreatitis-ards.care: Helps: Lung-protective ventilation (about 6 ml/kg predicted weight, plateau below 30), prone positioning, conservative fluids. Avoid: Large tidal volume, high driving pressure, fluid overload.

pancreatitis-ards.label: Hyaline membrane
pancreatitis-ards.title: Hyaline membrane
pancreatitis-ards.body: A pink film of plasma protein and dead cell debris lining the alveolus. It blocks gas exchange.
pancreatitis-ards.care: Helps: Lung-protective ventilation (about 6 ml/kg predicted weight, plateau below 30), prone positioning, conservative fluids. Avoid: Large tidal volume, high driving pressure, fluid overload.

pancreatitis-ards.label: Alveolar oedema
pancreatitis-ards.title: Oedema fluid
pancreatitis-ards.body: Leaky capillaries and a damaged epithelium let protein-rich fluid flood the air space.
pancreatitis-ards.care: Helps: Lung-protective ventilation (about 6 ml/kg predicted weight, plateau below 30), prone positioning, conservative fluids. Avoid: Large tidal volume, high driving pressure, fluid overload.

ards-baro.label: Apical bleb
ards-baro.title: Subpleural bleb
ards-baro.body: Air blebs at the apex rupture when peak or plateau pressure is high, letting air into the pleural space.
ards-baro.care: Helps: Plateau below 30 and driving pressure below 15, chest drain for a tension pneumothorax. Avoid: High tidal volume and PEEP beyond what oxygenation needs.

ards-baro.label: Air-leak cyst
ards-baro.title: Pneumatocele
ards-baro.body: A thin-walled air cyst that forms where overdistended lung tears. It can grow or rupture.
ards-baro.care: Helps: Lung-protective settings, watch for a new leak on the chest film. Avoid: Sudden pressure spikes (coughing, patient-ventilator asynchrony).

ards-baro.label: Air-filled space
ards-baro.title: Air-filled space
ards-baro.body: Gas has dissected out of the alveoli into the interstitium and beneath the pleura.
ards-baro.care: Helps: Lower pressures, drain if the leak is large. Avoid: High PEEP and tidal volume.

ards-baro.label: Overstretched wall
ards-baro.title: Alveolar epithelium
ards-baro.body: The thin alveolar wall is torn by overdistension. Air escapes into the tissue.
ards-baro.care: Helps: Lower driving pressure. Avoid: Volutrauma.

ards-fibro.label: Subpleural scarring
ards-fibro.title: Subpleural fibrosis
ards-fibro.body: Scar tissue forms at the periphery and bases first. The lung becomes stiff and shrinks.
ards-fibro.care: Helps: Early lung-protective ventilation, shorter ventilation, specialist review of persistent ARDS. Avoid: Long periods of high FiO2 and pressure.

ards-fibro.label: Honeycomb change
ards-fibro.title: Honeycombing
ards-fibro.body: Clustered thick-walled cysts mark late, established fibrosis. This part does not recover.
ards-fibro.care: Helps: Pulmonary rehabilitation, long-term follow-up. Avoid: Smoking and further lung injury.

ards-fibro.label: Fibrotic band
ards-fibro.title: Fibrotic band
ards-fibro.body: Pale, firm scar bands run through the cut face and distort the airways.
ards-fibro.care: Helps: Follow-up CT and lung function. Avoid: Assuming it will all reverse.

ards-fibro.label: Proliferating type II
ards-fibro.title: Type II cell
ards-fibro.body: Type II cells multiply to repair the wall. In prolonged injury fibroblasts follow and lay down collagen.
ards-fibro.care: Helps: Limit ventilator injury. Avoid: Prolonged high pressures.

ards-vap.label: Lower-lobe consolidation
ards-vap.title: Lower-lobe consolidation
ards-vap.body: Colonised secretions leak past the cuff to the dependent lower lobes and cause patchy pus-filled consolidation.
ards-vap.care: Helps: Head of bed 30 to 45 degrees, subglottic suction, daily sedation and ventilation review, early cultures and antibiotics by the local antibiogram. Avoid: Unnecessary sedation and prolonged intubation.

ards-vap.label: Second focus
ards-vap.title: Multifocal spread
ards-vap.body: Infection can involve several lobes. New or enlarging opacities, fever and purulent secretions raise the suspicion.
ards-vap.care: Helps: Sputum or tracheal aspirate culture, de-escalate when results return.

ards-vap.label: Pus in the airways
ards-vap.title: Pus in the airways
ards-vap.body: Yellow-green purulent plugs fill the bronchioles and surrounding alveoli.

ards-vap.label: Neutrophils
ards-vap.title: Neutrophil
ards-vap.body: Neutrophils flood the alveolus and release enzymes and oxygen radicals that injure the wall.

aki-pe.label: Perihilar oedema
aki-pe.title: Perihilar oedema
aki-pe.body: Fluid collects around the hila first and spreads outward, the 'bat-wing' pattern on a chest film.
aki-pe.care: Helps: Fluid removal (diuretic if responsive, ultrafiltration or dialysis), CPAP or NIV, treat hyperkalaemia. Avoid: More intravenous fluid.

aki-pe.label: Basal oedema
aki-pe.title: Basal oedema
aki-pe.body: Gravity loads the lower zones. Pleural effusions often sit beside it.
aki-pe.care: Helps: Fluid removal (diuretic if responsive, ultrafiltration or dialysis), CPAP or NIV, treat hyperkalaemia. Avoid: More intravenous fluid.

aki-pe.label: Frothy fluid
aki-pe.title: Frothy fluid
aki-pe.body: The cut face oozes thin, pink, frothy fluid because the capillaries are overloaded with volume.
aki-pe.care: Helps: Fluid removal (diuretic if responsive, ultrafiltration or dialysis), CPAP or NIV, treat hyperkalaemia. Avoid: More intravenous fluid.

aki-pe.label: Oedema fluid
aki-pe.title: Oedema fluid
aki-pe.body: Fluid fills the air space. Here it comes from volume overload with no way to pass urine.
aki-pe.care: Helps: Fluid removal (diuretic if responsive, ultrafiltration or dialysis), CPAP or NIV, treat hyperkalaemia. Avoid: More intravenous fluid.

ahf-pe.label: Perihilar oedema
ahf-pe.title: Perihilar oedema
ahf-pe.body: Fluid collects around the hila first and spreads outward, the 'bat-wing' pattern on a chest film.
ahf-pe.care: Helps: Intravenous loop diuretic, vasodilator if blood pressure allows, CPAP or NIV, treat the cause. Avoid: Fluid boluses.

ahf-pe.label: Basal oedema
ahf-pe.title: Basal oedema
ahf-pe.body: Gravity loads the lower zones. Pleural effusions often sit beside it.
ahf-pe.care: Helps: Intravenous loop diuretic, vasodilator if blood pressure allows, CPAP or NIV, treat the cause. Avoid: Fluid boluses.

ahf-pe.label: Frothy fluid
ahf-pe.title: Frothy fluid
ahf-pe.body: The cut face oozes pink, frothy fluid pushed out by a high left atrial pressure.
ahf-pe.care: Helps: Intravenous loop diuretic, vasodilator if blood pressure allows, CPAP or NIV, treat the cause. Avoid: Fluid boluses.

ahf-pe.label: Oedema fluid
ahf-pe.title: Oedema fluid
ahf-pe.body: Fluid fills the air space. Here it comes from a high left atrial pressure that pushes fluid out of the capillaries.
ahf-pe.care: Helps: Intravenous loop diuretic, vasodilator if blood pressure allows, CPAP or NIV, treat the cause. Avoid: Fluid boluses.

tbi-npe.label: Perihilar oedema
tbi-npe.title: Perihilar oedema
tbi-npe.body: Fluid collects around the hila first and spreads outward, the 'bat-wing' pattern on a chest film.
tbi-npe.care: Helps: Treat the brain injury and ICP, lung-protective ventilation, avoid fluid overload. Avoid: Large fluid boluses and high tidal volume.

tbi-npe.label: Basal oedema
tbi-npe.title: Basal oedema
tbi-npe.body: Gravity loads the lower zones. Pleural effusions often sit beside it.
tbi-npe.care: Helps: Treat the brain injury and ICP, lung-protective ventilation, avoid fluid overload. Avoid: Large fluid boluses and high tidal volume.

tbi-npe.label: Frothy fluid
tbi-npe.title: Frothy fluid
tbi-npe.body: The cut face is wet with blood-tinged frothy fluid from a sudden catecholamine surge.
tbi-npe.care: Helps: Treat the brain injury and ICP, lung-protective ventilation, avoid fluid overload. Avoid: Large fluid boluses and high tidal volume.

tbi-npe.label: Oedema fluid
tbi-npe.title: Oedema fluid
tbi-npe.body: Fluid fills the air space. Here a catecholamine surge from the injured brain raises capillary pressure and permeability.
tbi-npe.care: Helps: Treat the brain injury and ICP, lung-protective ventilation, avoid fluid overload. Avoid: Large fluid boluses and high tidal volume.

status-asp.label: Aspiration focus
status-asp.title: Aspiration focus
status-asp.body: Gastric contents run to the right lower lobe and the posterior upper lobes. Acid burns the lining and bacteria follow.
status-asp.care: Helps: Airway protection, suction, oxygen, antibiotics only if infection is likely. Avoid: Routine steroids and prophylactic antibiotics for chemical pneumonitis.

status-asp.label: Posterior segment
status-asp.title: Posterior upper lobe
status-asp.body: A patient lying on their back aspirates into the posterior segments.
status-asp.care: Helps: Early airway control during prolonged seizures.

status-asp.label: Acid injury
status-asp.title: Acid injury
status-asp.body: Dark, haemorrhagic and oedematous lung where acid and food particles landed.

status-asp.label: Alveolar oedema
status-asp.title: Oedema fluid
status-asp.body: Acid destroys the lining. Fluid and neutrophils pour in within hours.

ards-rv.label: Dilated right ventricle
ards-rv.title: Dilated right ventricle
ards-rv.body: High lung vascular resistance overloads the thin right ventricle. It dilates and bulges forward.
ards-rv.care: Helps: Lung-protective ventilation, prone positioning, inhaled nitric oxide or prostacyclin. Avoid: Excess PEEP and plateau pressure, large fluid bolus.

ards-rv.label: Septal shift
ards-rv.title: Bowed septum
ards-rv.body: The septum bows toward the left ventricle, so left filling and cardiac output fall.
ards-rv.care: Helps: Reduce RV afterload, norepinephrine to protect coronary perfusion. Avoid: Hypoxia and hypercapnia, which raise pulmonary resistance.

ards-rv.label: Large thin-walled RV
ards-rv.title: Large thin-walled right ventricle
ards-rv.body: The right cavity is large and the wall thin. The flattened septum squeezes the left ventricle (D-shaped left ventricle).
ards-rv.care: Helps: Echo to track RV size and septum.

ards-rv.label: Stretched myocyte
ards-rv.title: Cardiomyocyte
ards-rv.body: RV muscle cells are over-stretched and their coronary supply falls under pressure. Force of contraction drops.

aki-hyperk.label: Conduction system
aki-hyperk.title: Conduction slowing
aki-hyperk.body: High potassium depolarises cells and slows conduction. The ECG shows peaked T waves, a wide QRS and then a sine wave.
aki-hyperk.care: Helps: Calcium (membrane protection), insulin with glucose, salbutamol, dialysis for removal. Avoid: Potassium-containing fluids and drugs, delay.

aki-hyperk.label: Ventricular irritability
aki-hyperk.title: Ventricular irritability
aki-hyperk.body: The ventricle becomes prone to fibrillation as the potassium rises.
aki-hyperk.care: Helps: Early calcium and urgent potassium removal.

aki-hyperk.label: Pale slack ventricle
aki-hyperk.title: Pale ventricle
aki-hyperk.body: The wall contracts poorly when potassium is very high.
aki-hyperk.care: Helps: Treat the potassium, then the cause.

aki-hyperk.label: Depolarised myocyte
aki-hyperk.title: Cardiomyocyte
aki-hyperk.body: Extracellular potassium rises, so the resting membrane potential moves toward threshold and sodium channels inactivate.
aki-hyperk.care: Helps: Calcium stabilises the membrane; insulin and beta agonists shift potassium into cells.

ahf-cs.label: Failing left ventricle
ahf-cs.title: Failing left ventricle
ahf-cs.body: A large, poorly contracting left ventricle cannot maintain output. Blood pressure falls despite high filling pressures.
ahf-cs.care: Helps: Revascularise if ischaemic, inotrope or vasopressor, mechanical support if refractory. Avoid: Fluid boluses and vasodilators that drop pressure.

ahf-cs.label: Ischaemic territory
ahf-cs.title: Ischaemic territory
ahf-cs.body: In an infarct, the damaged territory (often the anterior wall) is pale and akinetic.

ahf-cs.label: Dilated, thin wall
ahf-cs.title: Dilated left ventricle
ahf-cs.body: A dilated cavity with a thin, poorly contracting wall. Output is low.

ahf-cs.label: Energy-starved myocyte
ahf-cs.title: Mitochondrion
ahf-cs.body: Mitochondria swell and the cell runs out of ATP. Contraction fades.
ahf-cs.care: Helps: Restore coronary flow and oxygen delivery.

ahf-arr.label: Atrial stretch
ahf-arr.title: Atrial stretch
ahf-arr.body: A high filling pressure stretches the atria and starts atrial fibrillation, which takes away the atrial kick.
ahf-arr.care: Helps: Rate or rhythm control, cardioversion if unstable, correct potassium and magnesium. Avoid: Starting negative inotropes in decompensated failure.

ahf-arr.label: Ventricular scar
ahf-arr.title: Ventricular scar
ahf-arr.body: Scar and stretched myocardium give re-entry circuits, so ventricular tachycardia can start.
ahf-arr.care: Helps: Amiodarone, defibrillation for VT or VF, ICD later. Avoid: Pro-arrhythmic drugs and electrolyte disturbances.

ahf-arr.label: Remodelled wall
ahf-arr.title: Remodelled wall
ahf-arr.body: The dilated, patchy wall conducts unevenly, which allows re-entry.

ahf-arr.label: Beta receptor
ahf-arr.title: Beta receptor
ahf-arr.body: Chronic catecholamine drive down-regulates beta receptors and makes the membrane unstable.
ahf-arr.care: Helps: Beta-blocker when stable. Avoid: High-dose catecholamines.

cardiac.label: Dilated left ventricle
cardiac.title: Dilated left ventricle
cardiac.body: In sepsis the ventricle dilates and its ejection fraction falls. It usually recovers over 7 to 10 days.
cardiac.care: Helps: Dobutamine or levosimendan if low output with adequate pressure; avoid excess catecholamine. Avoid: High-dose adrenaline and unnecessary fluid.

cardiac.label: Right ventricle
cardiac.title: Right ventricle
cardiac.body: The right ventricle is also stunned, which is often missed.

cardiac.label: Dilated cavity
cardiac.title: Dilated cavity
cardiac.body: A dilated, thin-looking chamber with reduced wall thickening.

cardiac.label: Swollen mitochondria
cardiac.title: Mitochondrion
cardiac.body: Cytokines and nitric oxide impair mitochondria and calcium handling. This is stunning, not cell death.
cardiac.care: Helps: Treat sepsis and restore perfusion.

aki.label: Swollen pale cortex
aki.title: Swollen cortex
aki.body: The cortex swells and turns pale as flow falls and tubular cells die.
aki.care: Helps: Restore perfusion and MAP, stop nephrotoxins, treat the cause, renal replacement for refractory acidosis, hyperkalaemia, overload or uraemia. Avoid: NSAIDs, contrast, aminoglycosides when avoidable, and further fluid overload.

aki.label: Medullary congestion
aki.title: Medullary congestion
aki.body: The outer medulla is the most hypoxic zone and is dark and congested in injury.
aki.care: Helps: Restore perfusion and MAP, stop nephrotoxins, treat the cause, renal replacement for refractory acidosis, hyperkalaemia, overload or uraemia. Avoid: NSAIDs, contrast, aminoglycosides when avoidable, and further fluid overload.

aki.label: Pale cortex, dark medulla
aki.title: Pale cortex and dark medulla
aki.body: The cortex is pale and swollen while the medulla is dark and congested. This is acute tubular injury.
aki.care: Helps: Restore perfusion and MAP, stop nephrotoxins, treat the cause, renal replacement for refractory acidosis, hyperkalaemia, overload or uraemia. Avoid: NSAIDs, contrast, aminoglycosides when avoidable, and further fluid overload.

aki.label: Injured tubular cell
aki.title: Tubular cell
aki.body: Proximal tubular cells lose their brush border, swell and shed into the lumen.
aki.care: Helps: Restore perfusion and MAP, stop nephrotoxins, treat the cause, renal replacement for refractory acidosis, hyperkalaemia, overload or uraemia. Avoid: NSAIDs, contrast, aminoglycosides when avoidable, and further fluid overload.

aki.label: Casts
aki.title: Cast
aki.body: Dead cells and protein plug the tubule and raise upstream pressure, so filtration falls.
aki.care: Helps: Restore perfusion and MAP, stop nephrotoxins, treat the cause, renal replacement for refractory acidosis, hyperkalaemia, overload or uraemia. Avoid: NSAIDs, contrast, aminoglycosides when avoidable, and further fluid overload.

pancreatitis-aki.label: Swollen pale cortex
pancreatitis-aki.title: Swollen cortex
pancreatitis-aki.body: Hypovolaemia and inflammation starve the cortex. It is swollen and pale.
pancreatitis-aki.care: Helps: Early goal-directed fluid resuscitation with balanced crystalloid, avoid nephrotoxins, watch for abdominal compartment syndrome. Avoid: NSAIDs and aggressive over-resuscitation.

pancreatitis-aki.label: Medullary congestion
pancreatitis-aki.title: Medullary congestion
pancreatitis-aki.body: The outer medulla is the most hypoxic zone and is dark and congested in injury.
pancreatitis-aki.care: Helps: Early goal-directed fluid resuscitation with balanced crystalloid, avoid nephrotoxins, watch for abdominal compartment syndrome. Avoid: NSAIDs and aggressive over-resuscitation.

pancreatitis-aki.label: Pale cortex, dark medulla
pancreatitis-aki.title: Pale cortex and dark medulla
pancreatitis-aki.body: The cortex is pale and swollen while the medulla is dark. Poor perfusion drives tubular injury.
pancreatitis-aki.care: Helps: Early goal-directed fluid resuscitation with balanced crystalloid, avoid nephrotoxins, watch for abdominal compartment syndrome. Avoid: NSAIDs and aggressive over-resuscitation.

pancreatitis-aki.label: Injured tubular cell
pancreatitis-aki.title: Tubular cell
pancreatitis-aki.body: Tubular cells lose their brush border and slough off.
pancreatitis-aki.care: Helps: Early goal-directed fluid resuscitation with balanced crystalloid, avoid nephrotoxins, watch for abdominal compartment syndrome. Avoid: NSAIDs and aggressive over-resuscitation.

pancreatitis-aki.label: Casts
pancreatitis-aki.title: Cast
pancreatitis-aki.body: Dead cells and protein plug the tubule and raise upstream pressure, so filtration falls.
pancreatitis-aki.care: Helps: Early goal-directed fluid resuscitation with balanced crystalloid, avoid nephrotoxins, watch for abdominal compartment syndrome. Avoid: NSAIDs and aggressive over-resuscitation.

aki-acid.label: Swollen pale cortex
aki-acid.title: Swollen cortex
aki-acid.body: The cortex swells. Damaged tubules cannot secrete hydrogen ions or reclaim bicarbonate.
aki-acid.care: Helps: Treat the cause, dialysis for severe acidosis, bicarbonate only for selected cases. Avoid: Excess chloride.

aki-acid.label: Medullary congestion
aki-acid.title: Medullary congestion
aki-acid.body: The outer medulla is the most hypoxic zone and is dark and congested in injury.
aki-acid.care: Helps: Treat the cause, dialysis for severe acidosis, bicarbonate only for selected cases. Avoid: Excess chloride.

aki-acid.label: Pale cortex, dark medulla
aki-acid.title: Pale cortex and dark medulla
aki-acid.body: Pale cortex, dark medulla. Failed tubules cannot excrete acid.
aki-acid.care: Helps: Treat the cause, dialysis for severe acidosis, bicarbonate only for selected cases. Avoid: Excess chloride.

aki-acid.label: Injured tubular cell
aki-acid.title: Tubular cell
aki-acid.body: Tubular cells lose bicarbonate reclamation and acid secretion, so the metabolic acidosis deepens.
aki-acid.care: Helps: Treat the cause, dialysis for severe acidosis, bicarbonate only for selected cases. Avoid: Excess chloride.

aki-acid.label: Casts
aki-acid.title: Cast
aki-acid.body: Dead cells and protein plug the tubule and raise upstream pressure, so filtration falls.
aki-acid.care: Helps: Treat the cause, dialysis for severe acidosis, bicarbonate only for selected cases. Avoid: Excess chloride.

aki-uremia.label: Swollen pale cortex
aki-uremia.title: Swollen cortex
aki-uremia.body: A swollen, congested kidney that cannot clear urea and toxins.
aki-uremia.care: Helps: Renal replacement for uraemic complications (encephalopathy, pericarditis, bleeding). Avoid: Delay when there are complications.

aki-uremia.label: Medullary congestion
aki-uremia.title: Medullary congestion
aki-uremia.body: The outer medulla is the most hypoxic zone and is dark and congested in injury.
aki-uremia.care: Helps: Renal replacement for uraemic complications (encephalopathy, pericarditis, bleeding). Avoid: Delay when there are complications.

aki-uremia.label: Pale cortex, dark medulla
aki-uremia.title: Pale cortex and dark medulla
aki-uremia.body: The cut face is pale and congested. Filtration has failed.
aki-uremia.care: Helps: Renal replacement for uraemic complications (encephalopathy, pericarditis, bleeding). Avoid: Delay when there are complications.

aki-uremia.label: Injured tubular cell
aki-uremia.title: Tubular cell
aki-uremia.body: Tubular injury and low filtration let urea and toxins accumulate.
aki-uremia.care: Helps: Renal replacement for uraemic complications (encephalopathy, pericarditis, bleeding). Avoid: Delay when there are complications.

aki-uremia.label: Casts
aki-uremia.title: Cast
aki-uremia.body: Dead cells and protein plug the tubule and raise upstream pressure, so filtration falls.
aki-uremia.care: Helps: Renal replacement for uraemic complications (encephalopathy, pericarditis, bleeding). Avoid: Delay when there are complications.

alf-hrs.label: Swollen pale cortex
alf-hrs.title: Swollen cortex
alf-hrs.body: Structurally the cortex is near normal but starved of flow by splanchnic vasodilation.
alf-hrs.care: Helps: Albumin, terlipressin or norepinephrine, treat infection and bleeding, transplant assessment. Avoid: Nephrotoxins and large-volume paracentesis without albumin.

alf-hrs.label: Medullary congestion
alf-hrs.title: Medullary congestion
alf-hrs.body: The outer medulla is the most hypoxic zone and is dark and congested in injury.
alf-hrs.care: Helps: Albumin, terlipressin or norepinephrine, treat infection and bleeding, transplant assessment. Avoid: Nephrotoxins and large-volume paracentesis without albumin.

alf-hrs.label: Pale cortex, dark medulla
alf-hrs.title: Pale cortex and dark medulla
alf-hrs.body: A kidney that looks structurally normal on the cut face but makes almost no urine, because the problem is flow, not damage.
alf-hrs.care: Helps: Albumin, terlipressin or norepinephrine, treat infection and bleeding, transplant assessment. Avoid: Nephrotoxins and large-volume paracentesis without albumin.

alf-hrs.label: Injured tubular cell
alf-hrs.title: Tubular cell
alf-hrs.body: Tubular cells are intact but under-perfused. This is why hepatorenal AKI can recover if flow is restored.
alf-hrs.care: Helps: Albumin, terlipressin or norepinephrine, treat infection and bleeding, transplant assessment. Avoid: Nephrotoxins and large-volume paracentesis without albumin.

alf-hrs.label: Casts
alf-hrs.title: Cast
alf-hrs.body: Dead cells and protein plug the tubule and raise upstream pressure, so filtration falls.
alf-hrs.care: Helps: Albumin, terlipressin or norepinephrine, treat infection and bleeding, transplant assessment. Avoid: Nephrotoxins and large-volume paracentesis without albumin.

ahf-aki.label: Swollen pale cortex
ahf-aki.title: Swollen cortex
ahf-aki.body: Venous congestion and low output reduce renal perfusion pressure. The kidney is swollen and blue-pink.
ahf-aki.care: Helps: Decongest with diuretic or ultrafiltration, restore output, avoid hypotension. Avoid: Fluid boluses and NSAIDs.

ahf-aki.label: Medullary congestion
ahf-aki.title: Medullary congestion
ahf-aki.body: The outer medulla is the most hypoxic zone and is dark and congested in injury.
ahf-aki.care: Helps: Decongest with diuretic or ultrafiltration, restore output, avoid hypotension. Avoid: Fluid boluses and NSAIDs.

ahf-aki.label: Pale cortex, dark medulla
ahf-aki.title: Pale cortex and dark medulla
ahf-aki.body: A congested, swollen kidney. Venous hypertension is as harmful as low flow.
ahf-aki.care: Helps: Decongest with diuretic or ultrafiltration, restore output, avoid hypotension. Avoid: Fluid boluses and NSAIDs.

ahf-aki.label: Injured tubular cell
ahf-aki.title: Tubular cell
ahf-aki.body: Tubular cells are hypoxic and under pressure from venous congestion.
ahf-aki.care: Helps: Decongest with diuretic or ultrafiltration, restore output, avoid hypotension. Avoid: Fluid boluses and NSAIDs.

ahf-aki.label: Casts
ahf-aki.title: Cast
ahf-aki.body: Dead cells and protein plug the tubule and raise upstream pressure, so filtration falls.
ahf-aki.care: Helps: Decongest with diuretic or ultrafiltration, restore output, avoid hypotension. Avoid: Fluid boluses and NSAIDs.

dic-aki.label: Swollen pale cortex
dic-aki.title: Swollen cortex
dic-aki.body: Micro-thrombi in the glomerular capillaries and a failing circulation injure the kidney.
dic-aki.care: Helps: Treat the trigger, replace factors if bleeding, supportive care. Avoid: Nephrotoxins.

dic-aki.label: Medullary congestion
dic-aki.title: Medullary congestion
dic-aki.body: The outer medulla is the most hypoxic zone and is dark and congested in injury.
dic-aki.care: Helps: Treat the trigger, replace factors if bleeding, supportive care. Avoid: Nephrotoxins.

dic-aki.label: Pale cortex, dark medulla
dic-aki.title: Pale cortex and dark medulla
dic-aki.body: Pale cortex with small haemorrhagic spots, from fibrin plugs in the glomeruli.
dic-aki.care: Helps: Treat the trigger, replace factors if bleeding, supportive care. Avoid: Nephrotoxins.

dic-aki.label: Injured tubular cell
dic-aki.title: Tubular cell
dic-aki.body: Tubular cells die from ischaemia downstream of the blocked capillaries.
dic-aki.care: Helps: Treat the trigger, replace factors if bleeding, supportive care. Avoid: Nephrotoxins.

dic-aki.label: Casts
dic-aki.title: Cast
dic-aki.body: Dead cells and protein plug the tubule and raise upstream pressure, so filtration falls.
dic-aki.care: Helps: Treat the trigger, replace factors if bleeding, supportive care. Avoid: Nephrotoxins.

dka-kidney.label: Swollen pale cortex
dka-kidney.title: Swollen cortex
dka-kidney.body: Osmotic diuresis dries the patient out and lowers renal perfusion. The kidney is pale and small.
dka-kidney.care: Helps: Isotonic fluid then insulin infusion, potassium replacement once urine flows and K is below the threshold. Avoid: Insulin before potassium is known.

dka-kidney.label: Medullary congestion
dka-kidney.title: Medullary congestion
dka-kidney.body: The outer medulla is the most hypoxic zone and is dark and congested in injury.
dka-kidney.care: Helps: Isotonic fluid then insulin infusion, potassium replacement once urine flows and K is below the threshold. Avoid: Insulin before potassium is known.

dka-kidney.label: Pale cortex, dark medulla
dka-kidney.title: Pale cortex and dark medulla
dka-kidney.body: Pre-renal pattern: the cut face is pale but structurally intact.
dka-kidney.care: Helps: Isotonic fluid then insulin infusion, potassium replacement once urine flows and K is below the threshold. Avoid: Insulin before potassium is known.

dka-kidney.label: Injured tubular cell
dka-kidney.title: Tubular cell
dka-kidney.body: Tubular cells face a heavy glucose and ketone load and lose water and salts.
dka-kidney.care: Helps: Isotonic fluid then insulin infusion, potassium replacement once urine flows and K is below the threshold. Avoid: Insulin before potassium is known.

dka-kidney.label: Casts
dka-kidney.title: Cast
dka-kidney.body: Dead cells and protein plug the tubule and raise upstream pressure, so filtration falls.
dka-kidney.care: Helps: Isotonic fluid then insulin infusion, potassium replacement once urine flows and K is below the threshold. Avoid: Insulin before potassium is known.

hepatic.label: Congested, swollen liver
hepatic.title: Swollen congested liver
hepatic.body: Sepsis enlarges and congests the liver. Cholestasis, fat and, in shock, hypoxic necrosis can all be present.
hepatic.care: Helps: Restore perfusion, source control, avoid overfeeding. Avoid: Hepatotoxic drugs (excess paracetamol, amiodarone) and long fasts.

hepatic.label: Gallbladder
hepatic.title: Gallbladder
hepatic.body: Acalculous cholecystitis can accompany severe sepsis. Cholestasis alone does not mean a blocked duct.
hepatic.care: Helps: Ultrasound only if the picture suggests biliary sepsis.

hepatic.label: Central necrosis
hepatic.title: Centrilobular necrosis
hepatic.body: Zone 3 cells around the central vein lie farthest from oxygen and die first in shock (hypoxic hepatitis).
hepatic.care: Helps: Restore cardiac output and oxygen delivery. Avoid: Hypotension.

hepatic.label: Bile salts retained
hepatic.title: Hepatocyte
hepatic.body: Cytokines down-regulate bile-salt transporters, so bilirubin and bile acids spill into the blood.
hepatic.care: Helps: Treat the sepsis; cholestasis reverses with it.

hepatic.label: Slow sinusoid flow
hepatic.title: Sinusoid
hepatic.body: Shock slows sinusoidal flow. Central hepatocytes are the first to starve.
hepatic.care: Helps: Maintain MAP and cardiac output.

alf-hypoglyc.label: Necrotic liver
alf-hypoglyc.title: Necrotic liver
alf-hypoglyc.body: Massive hepatocyte loss leaves a mottled, shrunken liver that can no longer make glucose.
alf-hypoglyc.care: Helps: Glucose infusion and hourly checks, urgent transplant assessment. Avoid: Prolonged fasting and insulin without glucose.

alf-hypoglyc.label: Atrophic left lobe
alf-hypoglyc.title: Shrunken lobe
alf-hypoglyc.body: A small, soft liver on imaging signals extensive necrosis.

alf-hypoglyc.label: Mottled necrosis
alf-hypoglyc.title: Mottled necrosis
alf-hypoglyc.body: Patches of dead and surviving tissue. Glycogen stores are gone and gluconeogenesis fails.

alf-hypoglyc.label: Failed gluconeogenesis
alf-hypoglyc.title: Hepatocyte
alf-hypoglyc.body: Dying hepatocytes cannot release glycogen or make new glucose, so the blood sugar falls.
alf-hypoglyc.care: Helps: 10 to 20% dextrose by central line, monitor hourly.

dka-meta.label: Fatty, ketogenic liver
dka-meta.title: Fatty, ketogenic liver
dka-meta.body: Low insulin and high glucagon send fat to the liver, which turns it into ketones.
dka-meta.care: Helps: Fixed-rate insulin infusion with fluids and potassium. Avoid: Stopping insulin while ketones are still present.

dka-meta.label: Fat-laden tissue
dka-meta.title: Fat-laden tissue
dka-meta.body: Fatty change and depleted glycogen, from hormone imbalance rather than primary liver failure.
dka-meta.care: Helps: Treat the cause and restore insulin.

dka-meta.label: Ketone production
dka-meta.title: Hepatocyte
dka-meta.body: Beta-oxidation is unchecked, so acetyl-CoA is made into acetoacetate and beta-hydroxybutyrate. The anion gap rises.
dka-meta.care: Helps: Insulin switches off ketogenesis. Avoid: Bicarbonate unless pH is severely low.

enceph.label: Diffuse cortical dysfunction
enceph.title: Diffuse dysfunction
enceph.body: Both hemispheres are affected. There is no focal lesion. EEG is slow and the patient is drowsy or delirious.
enceph.care: Helps: Restore pressure and oxygen, correct glucose and sodium, avoid benzodiazepines, dexmedetomidine if sedation is needed. Avoid: Unrecognised cefepime neurotoxicity in renal failure.

enceph.label: Cerebellum
enceph.title: Cerebellum
enceph.body: Also swept up in the same diffuse process. Focal signs should prompt imaging.
enceph.care: Helps: CT or MRI if the signs are focal or sudden.

enceph.label: Mild diffuse oedema
enceph.title: Mild oedema
enceph.body: A slightly swollen brain with no focal mass. Microvascular injury is the cause.

enceph.label: Leaky barrier
enceph.title: Tight junction
enceph.body: Cytokines open the tight junctions, so protein and mediators enter the brain.

enceph.label: Swollen end-foot
enceph.title: Astrocyte end-foot
enceph.body: Astrocyte end-feet swell and loosen their grip on the capillary.

enceph.label: Quiet neurone
enceph.title: Neuron
enceph.body: Firing slows and desynchronises. The cell is not destroyed.

alf-cedema.label: Flattened gyri
alf-cedema.title: Flattened gyri
alf-cedema.body: Swelling presses the gyri against the skull and fills the sulci. Intracranial pressure rises.
alf-cedema.care: Helps: Head-up 30 degrees, keep sodium 145 to 155, hypertonic saline or mannitol, treat ammonia (early renal replacement), avoid fever. Avoid: Hypotonic fluids, hyponatraemia, sedation that hides the examination.

alf-cedema.label: Tonsillar pressure
alf-cedema.title: Tonsillar pressure
alf-cedema.body: Raised pressure pushes the cerebellar tonsils toward the foramen magnum.
alf-cedema.care: Helps: Urgent ICP treatment and neurocritical care review.

alf-cedema.label: Effaced sulci
alf-cedema.title: Effaced sulci and ventricles
alf-cedema.body: The grey-white boundary blurs and the ventricles are squeezed as the brain swells.
alf-cedema.care: Helps: Serial CT or ICP monitoring in high-risk patients.

alf-cedema.label: Swollen astrocyte
alf-cedema.title: Astrocyte end-foot
alf-cedema.body: Ammonia is turned into glutamine inside astrocytes. Glutamine draws water in, so the cells swell.

tbi-icp.label: Contusion
tbi-icp.title: Contusion
tbi-icp.body: Frontal and temporal poles bruise as the brain strikes bone. Surrounding oedema adds pressure.
tbi-icp.care: Helps: Head-up 30 degrees, avoid hypotension and hypoxia, osmotherapy, surgical decompression when indicated. Avoid: Hyperventilation except as a brief bridge.

tbi-icp.label: Swollen hemisphere
tbi-icp.title: Swollen hemisphere
tbi-icp.body: Raised pressure compresses the brain and reduces perfusion pressure (MAP minus ICP).
tbi-icp.care: Helps: Keep CPP near 60 to 70 mmHg. Avoid: Fluid that lowers sodium.

tbi-icp.label: Midline shift
tbi-icp.title: Midline shift
tbi-icp.body: Mass effect pushes the midline toward the opposite side. A shift is a surgical warning sign.

tbi-icp.label: Swollen neurone
tbi-icp.title: Neuron
tbi-icp.body: Energy failure and glutamate excitotoxicity swell cells and raise pressure.
tbi-icp.care: Helps: Maintain oxygen and glucose delivery.

tbi-hern.label: Uncal herniation
tbi-hern.title: Uncal herniation
tbi-hern.body: The medial temporal lobe slips past the tentorium and squeezes the third nerve and brainstem. The pupil dilates.
tbi-hern.care: Helps: Immediate hyperosmolar therapy, brief hyperventilation as a bridge, urgent surgery. Avoid: Delay.

tbi-hern.label: Tonsillar herniation
tbi-hern.title: Tonsillar herniation
tbi-hern.body: The cerebellar tonsils plug the foramen magnum and compress the medulla. Breathing stops.

tbi-hern.label: Midline shift
tbi-hern.title: Midline shift
tbi-hern.body: A large shift with compressed ventricles precedes herniation.

tbi-hern.label: Compressed neurone
tbi-hern.title: Neuron
tbi-hern.body: Brainstem neurones lose perfusion under compression. This causes the Cushing response and then loss of drive.
tbi-hern.care: Helps: Restore perfusion by lowering pressure.

tbi-isch.label: Watershed zone
tbi-isch.title: Watershed zone
tbi-isch.body: The boundary between arterial territories is hit first when perfusion falls.
tbi-isch.care: Helps: Maintain CPP, avoid hypotension, hypoxia and hypocapnia. Avoid: Low MAP.

tbi-isch.label: Infarcted cortex
tbi-isch.title: Pale infarcted cortex
tbi-isch.body: The cortex turns pale and soft where flow has failed.

tbi-isch.label: Pale infarct
tbi-isch.title: Pale infarct
tbi-isch.body: A wedge of pale, swollen tissue lies in the territory of the failed artery.

tbi-isch.label: Starved neurone
tbi-isch.title: Neuron
tbi-isch.body: Without oxygen and glucose the cell fails its pumps and swells, then dies.

status-inj.label: Medial temporal lobe
status-inj.title: Medial temporal lobe
status-inj.body: The hippocampus is especially vulnerable to prolonged seizures.
status-inj.care: Helps: Stop seizures fast (benzodiazepine, then second-line, then anaesthetic if refractory), treat the cause. Avoid: Delay.

status-inj.label: Cortical injury
status-inj.title: Cortical injury
status-inj.body: Prolonged firing injures the cortex diffusely.
status-inj.care: Helps: Early seizure control, check glucose and sodium.

status-inj.label: Swollen cortex
status-inj.title: Swollen cortex
status-inj.body: Cytotoxic oedema swells the grey matter and blurs the boundary with white matter.

status-inj.label: Excitotoxic neurone
status-inj.title: Neuron
status-inj.body: Sustained firing floods the cell with calcium and glutamate injures it. Cell death follows after prolonged seizures.
status-inj.care: Helps: Early termination of the seizure.

dka-brain.label: Swollen brain
dka-brain.title: Swollen brain
dka-brain.body: Cerebral oedema is uncommon in DKA but can be fatal, mostly in children and after fluid or rapid osmolar shifts.
dka-brain.care: Helps: Gradual correction, mannitol or hypertonic saline at the first sign, head-up. Avoid: Fluid boluses, falls in glucose faster than 5 mmol/L per hour, bicarbonate.

dka-brain.label: Effaced sulci
dka-brain.title: Effaced sulci
dka-brain.body: The sulci narrow and the ventricles shrink as the brain swells.

dka-brain.label: Swollen astrocyte
dka-brain.title: Astrocyte end-foot
dka-brain.body: Rapid fall in plasma osmolality draws water into brain cells.

dic.label: Fibrin plugs
dic.title: Fibrin plugs
dic.body: Thrombin generation lays fibrin in small vessels and blocks flow to tissue.
dic.care: Helps: Treat the cause, give platelets and FFP only if bleeding. Avoid: Tranexamic acid without a clear indication.

dic.label: Fibrin mesh
dic.title: Fibrin strand
dic.body: Cross-linked fibrin traps platelets and red cells, forming microthrombi.
dic.care: Helps: Source control. Heparin only for thrombotic DIC.

dic.label: Tissue factor displayed
dic.title: Endothelium
dic.body: In sepsis the endothelium and monocytes display tissue factor. That starts the clotting cascade.

shock.label: Dilated arteriole
shock.title: Dilated arteriole
shock.body: Nitric oxide and low vasopressin vasodilate vessels. Pressure falls despite adequate flow.
shock.care: Helps: Fluids, then noradrenaline, add vasopressin, then hydrocortisone if still low. Avoid: Excess fluid.

shock.label: Leaky endothelium
shock.title: Endothelium
shock.body: The glycocalyx is shed. Protein and fluid leave the capillary.
shock.care: Helps: Treat the source. Avoid fluid overload.

pancreatitis-shock.label: Leaky vessel
pancreatitis-shock.title: Capillary leak
pancreatitis-shock.body: Inflammation and third-space fluid empty the circulation. Pressure falls.
pancreatitis-shock.care: Helps: Early balanced crystalloid, monitor urine output and lactate. Avoid: Both too little and too much fluid.

pancreatitis-shock.label: Leaky endothelium
pancreatitis-shock.title: Endothelium
pancreatitis-shock.body: The endothelium becomes permeable under inflammatory mediators, so plasma leaves the vessel.

alf-inf.label: Vasoplegia
alf-inf.title: Vasoplegic vessel
alf-inf.body: Liver failure removes immune and clearing functions and causes vasodilation. Infection and low systemic resistance follow.
alf-inf.care: Helps: Blood cultures, broad antibiotics, vasopressor, low threshold for antifungals. Avoid: Delay.

alf-inf.label: Vasodilated vessel
alf-inf.title: Endothelium
alf-inf.body: Inflammatory mediators and nitric oxide relax vessel walls.

status-hypox.label: Hypoxic vessel
status-hypox.title: Hypoxic vessel
status-hypox.body: During convulsions oxygen demand outstrips supply and the airway may be unprotected.
status-hypox.care: Helps: Airway, oxygen and early seizure control. Avoid: Delay in treatment.

status-hypox.label: Oxygen-starved endothelium
status-hypox.title: Endothelium
status-hypox.body: Hypoxia and acidosis injure the endothelium and raise permeability.

dic-thromb.label: Microthrombi
dic-thromb.title: Microthrombi
dic-thromb.body: Small clots block capillaries and starve tissue.
dic-thromb.care: Helps: Treat the trigger. Consider heparin only in clear thrombotic DIC.

dic-thromb.label: Damaged endothelium
dic-thromb.title: Endothelium
dic-thromb.body: A damaged lining exposes tissue factor and loses its natural anticoagulants.

dic-bleed.label: Haematoma
dic-bleed.title: Haematoma
dic-bleed.body: Blood pools and spreads because clotting factors and platelets are used up.
dic-bleed.care: Helps: Treat the cause. Platelets if below 50 with bleeding, FFP and fibrinogen for factor loss. Avoid: Giving products with no bleeding.

dic-bleed.label: Oozing site
dic-bleed.title: Oozing blood
dic-bleed.body: A slow ooze from every raw surface and puncture site.
dic-bleed.care: Helps: Replace factors and platelets for active bleeding.

dic-bleed.label: Gap in the wall
dic-bleed.title: Gap in the wall
dic-bleed.body: A hole with no platelet plug. Red cells escape.

dic-bleed.label: Missing platelets
dic-bleed.title: Platelet
dic-bleed.body: Platelets are consumed in clot formation, so none remain to seal the leak.
dic-bleed.care: Helps: Transfuse for bleeding or before procedures.

alf-coag.label: Haematoma
alf-coag.title: Haematoma
alf-coag.body: The liver no longer makes clotting factors. Tissue bleeds from minor trauma.
alf-coag.care: Helps: Vitamin K, treat bleeding with FFP, cryoprecipitate or factor concentrates. Avoid: Correcting INR without bleeding, because it is a prognostic marker.

alf-coag.label: Oozing site
alf-coag.title: Oozing blood
alf-coag.body: A slow ooze from line sites and mucosa.

alf-coag.label: Few platelets
alf-coag.title: Platelet
alf-coag.body: Low platelets and missing factors make the plug fragile.
alf-coag.care: Helps: Replace according to bleeding and procedure.

tbi-coag.label: Haematoma
tbi-coag.title: Haematoma
tbi-coag.body: Brain tissue factor released into the blood triggers coagulopathy. Bleeding into the brain can expand.
tbi-coag.care: Helps: Early correction of coagulopathy, tranexamic acid within 3 hours of injury, repeat CT. Avoid: Delay.

tbi-coag.label: Oozing site
tbi-coag.title: Oozing blood
tbi-coag.body: Ooze from the wound and the contusion.
tbi-coag.care: Helps: Replace platelets, fibrinogen and factors.

tbi-coag.label: Few platelets
tbi-coag.title: Platelet
tbi-coag.body: Platelets are used up and function badly after tissue injury.

dic-purp.label: Purpura
dic-purp.title: Purpura
dic-purp.body: Purple, non-blanching patches where small vessels are blocked by clot. They are the visible sign of DIC in skin.
dic-purp.care: Helps: Treat the cause, protein C concentrate in purpura fulminans, early antibiotics. Avoid: Delay.

dic-purp.label: Haemorrhagic bulla
dic-purp.title: Haemorrhagic bulla
dic-purp.body: A blood-filled blister over necrotic skin.
dic-purp.care: Helps: Debride once demarcated, wound care.

dic-purp.label: Microthrombus
dic-purp.title: Microthrombus
dic-purp.body: Fibrin and platelets plug the dermal vessel and starve the skin.
dic-purp.care: Helps: Treat the trigger, anticoagulation selectively.

dic-isch.label: Ischaemic segment
dic-isch.title: Ischaemic segment
dic-isch.body: A dusky purple-black bowel loop where flow has failed. The mucosa dies first, then the full wall.
dic-isch.care: Helps: Early surgical review, restore flow, source control, antibiotics. Avoid: Delay, high-dose vasopressors when possible.

dic-isch.label: Mesenteric artery
dic-isch.title: Mesenteric artery
dic-isch.body: Low flow, vasopressors or an embolus reduce flow here.
dic-isch.care: Helps: Optimise cardiac output, CT angiography.

dic-isch.label: Dying villus tip
dic-isch.title: Villus
dic-isch.body: The tip is farthest from the blood supply, so it dies first and the barrier fails.

pancreatitis-acs.label: Oedematous bowel
pancreatitis-acs.title: Oedematous bowel
pancreatitis-acs.body: Gut oedema and ascites raise intra-abdominal pressure above 20 mmHg with new organ failure.
pancreatitis-acs.care: Helps: Sedation and paralysis, nasogastric decompression, drain fluid, limit fluids, decompressive laparotomy if refractory. Avoid: Large positive fluid balance.

pancreatitis-acs.label: Mesenteric artery
pancreatitis-acs.title: Mesenteric artery
pancreatitis-acs.body: High abdominal pressure squeezes mesenteric flow.

pancreatitis-acs.label: Villus
pancreatitis-acs.title: Villus
pancreatitis-acs.body: Low flow starves the villus tips and damages the gut barrier.

pancreatitis-necro.label: Fat necrosis
pancreatitis-necro.title: Fat necrosis
pancreatitis-necro.body: Chalky white spots of calcium soap where lipase digests fat.
pancreatitis-necro.care: Helps: Supportive care, early enteral feeding, antibiotics only for infected necrosis. Avoid: Early necrosectomy.

pancreatitis-necro.label: Haemorrhagic necrosis
pancreatitis-necro.title: Haemorrhage
pancreatitis-necro.body: Enzymes erode vessels. Dark red wet patches carry a worse outlook.
pancreatitis-necro.care: Helps: Monitor haemoglobin, angiography for bleeding.

pancreatitis-necro.label: Peripancreatic fluid
pancreatitis-necro.title: Peripancreatic fluid
pancreatitis-necro.body: A sterile fluid collection that tracks along the retroperitoneum.
pancreatitis-necro.care: Helps: Drain only if infected or symptomatic.

pancreatitis-necro.label: Self-digesting acinus
pancreatitis-necro.title: Acinar cell
pancreatitis-necro.body: Enzymes switch on inside the cell and digest it.
pancreatitis-necro.care: Helps: Remove the trigger (stone or alcohol).

pancreatitis-necro.label: Zymogen granule
pancreatitis-necro.title: Zymogen granule
pancreatitis-necro.body: Granules fuse with lysosomes and trypsin activates.

pancreatitis-hypoca.label: Fat necrosis soaps
pancreatitis-hypoca.title: Fat necrosis
pancreatitis-hypoca.body: Fatty acids bind calcium into soaps, so the serum calcium falls.
pancreatitis-hypoca.care: Helps: Check calcium and magnesium, replace if symptomatic or QT is long. Avoid: Treating a low total calcium with a normal ionised value.

pancreatitis-hypoca.label: Calcium soap
pancreatitis-hypoca.title: Fat necrosis droplet
pancreatitis-hypoca.body: Free fatty acids bind calcium to form soaps.

pancreatitis-hypoca.label: Acinar cell
pancreatitis-hypoca.title: Acinar cell
pancreatitis-hypoca.body: Injured acinar cells release enzymes that digest peripancreatic fat.

status-rhabdo.label: Swollen muscle
status-rhabdo.title: Swollen muscle
status-rhabdo.body: Muscle swells inside a tight fascial sleeve. Pressure can compromise perfusion.
status-rhabdo.care: Helps: Early aggressive fluids to keep urine flowing, treat the seizure, check CK, potassium and creatinine. Avoid: Delay, nephrotoxins.

status-rhabdo.label: Tight fascia
status-rhabdo.title: Fascia
status-rhabdo.body: Swelling has nowhere to go. Compartment syndrome is possible.
status-rhabdo.care: Helps: Measure compartment pressure if tense.

status-rhabdo.label: Torn sarcolemma
status-rhabdo.title: Sarcolemma
status-rhabdo.body: The torn membrane lets CK, potassium and myoglobin into the blood.

status-rhabdo.label: Myoglobin
status-rhabdo.title: Myoglobin
status-rhabdo.body: Myoglobin blocks tubules and turns the urine tea-coloured.

ards-main.label: Dependent consolidation
ards-main.title: Dependent consolidation
ards-main.body: Fluid-filled and collapsed alveoli fill the back of the lung. Proning moves the load and recruits them.
ards-main.care: Helps: Low tidal volume, 6 ml per kg; Titrated PEEP; Prone positioning; Neuromuscular blockade in severe ARDS; Conservative fluids; VV ECMO for refractory hypoxaemia. Avoid: High tidal volume; Liberal fluids.

ards-main.label: Patchy ground glass
ards-main.title: Aerated 'baby lung'
ards-main.body: Only a small part of the lung is still open. Large breaths overdistend it.
ards-main.care: Helps: Low tidal volume, 6 ml per kg; Titrated PEEP; Prone positioning; Neuromuscular blockade in severe ARDS; Conservative fluids; VV ECMO for refractory hypoxaemia. Avoid: High tidal volume; Liberal fluids.

ards-main.label: Wet, heavy lung
ards-main.title: Wet, heavy lung
ards-main.body: A red, rubbery cut face that weeps frothy fluid. The lung weighs two to three times normal.
ards-main.care: Helps: Low tidal volume, 6 ml per kg; Titrated PEEP; Prone positioning; Neuromuscular blockade in severe ARDS; Conservative fluids; VV ECMO for refractory hypoxaemia. Avoid: High tidal volume; Liberal fluids.

ards-main.label: Hyaline membrane
ards-main.title: Hyaline membrane
ards-main.body: A pink film of plasma protein and cell debris that lines the air sac and blocks gas exchange.
ards-main.care: Helps: Low tidal volume, 6 ml per kg; Titrated PEEP; Prone positioning; Neuromuscular blockade in severe ARDS; Conservative fluids; VV ECMO for refractory hypoxaemia. Avoid: High tidal volume; Liberal fluids.

ards-main.label: Oedema fluid
ards-main.title: Oedema fluid
ards-main.body: Leaky capillaries and a damaged lining let protein-rich fluid flood the air space.
ards-main.care: Helps: Low tidal volume, 6 ml per kg; Titrated PEEP; Prone positioning; Neuromuscular blockade in severe ARDS; Conservative fluids; VV ECMO for refractory hypoxaemia. Avoid: High tidal volume; Liberal fluids.

aki-main.label: Swollen pale cortex
aki-main.title: Swollen pale cortex
aki-main.body: The cortex swells and pales as flow falls and tubular cells die.
aki-main.care: Helps: Treat the cause and restore perfusion; Balanced crystalloid if volume depleted; Stop nephrotoxins; Keep MAP at 65 or above; Renal replacement therapy. Avoid: NSAIDs; Aminoglycoside or contrast; Fluid overload.

aki-main.label: Medullary congestion
aki-main.title: Medullary congestion
aki-main.body: Blood pools in the oxygen-poor medulla, where injury starts.
aki-main.care: Helps: Treat the cause and restore perfusion; Balanced crystalloid if volume depleted; Stop nephrotoxins; Keep MAP at 65 or above; Renal replacement therapy. Avoid: NSAIDs; Aminoglycoside or contrast; Fluid overload.

aki-main.label: Pale cortex, dark medulla
aki-main.title: Pale cortex, dark medulla
aki-main.body: The classic acute tubular injury pattern on the cut face.
aki-main.care: Helps: Treat the cause and restore perfusion; Balanced crystalloid if volume depleted; Stop nephrotoxins; Keep MAP at 65 or above; Renal replacement therapy. Avoid: NSAIDs; Aminoglycoside or contrast; Fluid overload.

aki-main.label: Injured tubular cell
aki-main.title: Injured tubular cell
aki-main.body: The cell loses its brush border and its energy. It swells and sloughs into the lumen.
aki-main.care: Helps: Treat the cause and restore perfusion; Balanced crystalloid if volume depleted; Stop nephrotoxins; Keep MAP at 65 or above; Renal replacement therapy. Avoid: NSAIDs; Aminoglycoside or contrast; Fluid overload.

aki-main.label: Cast
aki-main.title: Cast
aki-main.body: Shed cells and protein form casts that block the tubule and stop filtration.
aki-main.care: Helps: Treat the cause and restore perfusion; Balanced crystalloid if volume depleted; Stop nephrotoxins; Keep MAP at 65 or above; Renal replacement therapy. Avoid: NSAIDs; Aminoglycoside or contrast; Fluid overload.

pancreatitis-main.label: Fat necrosis
pancreatitis-main.title: Fat necrosis
pancreatitis-main.body: Chalky white spots of calcium soap where lipase has digested the fat.
pancreatitis-main.care: Helps: Treat the cause; Moderate Ringer lactate; Early enteral feeding; Analgesia. Avoid: Aggressive fluid loading; Prophylactic antibiotics; Prolonged nil by mouth.

pancreatitis-main.label: Haemorrhagic necrosis
pancreatitis-main.title: Haemorrhagic necrosis
pancreatitis-main.body: Enzymes erode vessels. Dark red wet patches mark a severe attack.
pancreatitis-main.care: Helps: Treat the cause; Moderate Ringer lactate; Early enteral feeding; Analgesia. Avoid: Aggressive fluid loading; Prophylactic antibiotics; Prolonged nil by mouth.

pancreatitis-main.label: Peripancreatic fluid
pancreatitis-main.title: Peripancreatic fluid
pancreatitis-main.body: Inflammatory fluid tracks along the retroperitoneum around the gland.
pancreatitis-main.care: Helps: Treat the cause; Moderate Ringer lactate; Early enteral feeding; Analgesia. Avoid: Aggressive fluid loading; Prophylactic antibiotics; Prolonged nil by mouth.

pancreatitis-main.label: Self-digesting acinus
pancreatitis-main.title: Acinar cell
pancreatitis-main.body: Enzymes are switched on inside the cell and digest it.
pancreatitis-main.care: Helps: Treat the cause; Moderate Ringer lactate; Early enteral feeding; Analgesia. Avoid: Aggressive fluid loading; Prophylactic antibiotics; Prolonged nil by mouth.

pancreatitis-main.label: Zymogen granule
pancreatitis-main.title: Zymogen granule
pancreatitis-main.body: Granules fuse with lysosomes and trypsin activates too early.
pancreatitis-main.care: Helps: Treat the cause; Moderate Ringer lactate; Early enteral feeding; Analgesia. Avoid: Aggressive fluid loading; Prophylactic antibiotics; Prolonged nil by mouth.

alf-main.label: Necrotic liver
alf-main.title: Necrotic liver
alf-main.body: A soft, shrunken liver with a wrinkled capsule and yellow-green mottling.
alf-main.care: Helps: N-acetylcysteine; Remove the cause; Lactulose and ammonia control; Renal replacement for ammonia; Emergency transplant listing. Avoid: Late N-acetylcysteine; Sedatives and hepatotoxic drugs.

alf-main.label: Atrophic left lobe
alf-main.title: Atrophic left lobe
alf-main.body: Large areas of lost liver tissue leave a small, collapsed lobe.
alf-main.care: Helps: N-acetylcysteine; Remove the cause; Lactulose and ammonia control; Renal replacement for ammonia; Emergency transplant listing. Avoid: Late N-acetylcysteine; Sedatives and hepatotoxic drugs.

alf-main.label: Mottled necrosis
alf-main.title: Mottled necrosis
alf-main.body: Red, yellow and green patches of dead liver across the cut face.
alf-main.care: Helps: N-acetylcysteine; Remove the cause; Lactulose and ammonia control; Renal replacement for ammonia; Emergency transplant listing. Avoid: Late N-acetylcysteine; Sedatives and hepatotoxic drugs.

alf-main.label: Dying hepatocyte
alf-main.title: Dying hepatocyte
alf-main.body: The cell has lost its energy and glycogen and cannot clear ammonia.
alf-main.care: Helps: N-acetylcysteine; Remove the cause; Lactulose and ammonia control; Renal replacement for ammonia; Emergency transplant listing. Avoid: Late N-acetylcysteine; Sedatives and hepatotoxic drugs.

alf-main.label: Slow sinusoid flow
alf-main.title: Sinusoid
alf-main.body: Blood slows through the damaged sinusoids, so toxins are not cleared.
alf-main.care: Helps: N-acetylcysteine; Remove the cause; Lactulose and ammonia control; Renal replacement for ammonia; Emergency transplant listing. Avoid: Late N-acetylcysteine; Sedatives and hepatotoxic drugs.

ahf-main.label: Failing left ventricle
ahf-main.title: Failing left ventricle
ahf-main.body: A dilated, poorly contracting ventricle that forms the apex.
ahf-main.care: Helps: IV loop diuretic; Nitrate when blood pressure allows; Non-invasive ventilation; Treat the precipitant; Dobutamine in low output; Mechanical circulatory support. Avoid: Fluid bolus; Beta blocker in low output; NSAIDs.

ahf-main.label: Dilated right ventricle
ahf-main.title: Dilated right ventricle
ahf-main.body: Pressure backs up from the lungs and the right ventricle dilates.
ahf-main.care: Helps: IV loop diuretic; Nitrate when blood pressure allows; Non-invasive ventilation; Treat the precipitant; Dobutamine in low output; Mechanical circulatory support. Avoid: Fluid bolus; Beta blocker in low output; NSAIDs.

ahf-main.label: Dilated, thin wall
ahf-main.title: Dilated, thin wall
ahf-main.body: Enlarged cavities with a thin, pale wall and flattened trabeculae.
ahf-main.care: Helps: IV loop diuretic; Nitrate when blood pressure allows; Non-invasive ventilation; Treat the precipitant; Dobutamine in low output; Mechanical circulatory support. Avoid: Fluid bolus; Beta blocker in low output; NSAIDs.

ahf-main.label: Energy-starved myocyte
ahf-main.title: Energy-starved myocyte
ahf-main.body: Swollen mitochondria cannot make enough ATP to keep the cell squeezing.
ahf-main.care: Helps: IV loop diuretic; Nitrate when blood pressure allows; Non-invasive ventilation; Treat the precipitant; Dobutamine in low output; Mechanical circulatory support. Avoid: Fluid bolus; Beta blocker in low output; NSAIDs.

tbi-main.label: Contusion
tbi-main.title: Contusion
tbi-main.body: Bruised, haemorrhagic cortex under the impact and opposite it, often the frontal and temporal poles.
tbi-main.care: Helps: Head up 30 degrees; Hypertonic saline; Sedation and analgesia; CSF drainage; Evacuate a mass lesion; Keep CPP at 60 or above. Avoid: Hypotension; Hypotonic fluids; Hypoxia or hypercapnia.

tbi-main.label: Swollen hemisphere
tbi-main.title: Swollen hemisphere
tbi-main.body: Flattened gyri and tight sulci show a swollen hemisphere under pressure.
tbi-main.care: Helps: Head up 30 degrees; Hypertonic saline; Sedation and analgesia; CSF drainage; Evacuate a mass lesion; Keep CPP at 60 or above. Avoid: Hypotension; Hypotonic fluids; Hypoxia or hypercapnia.

tbi-main.label: Midline shift
tbi-main.title: Midline shift
tbi-main.body: The swollen side pushes the ventricles and the midline across.
tbi-main.care: Helps: Head up 30 degrees; Hypertonic saline; Sedation and analgesia; CSF drainage; Evacuate a mass lesion; Keep CPP at 60 or above. Avoid: Hypotension; Hypotonic fluids; Hypoxia or hypercapnia.

tbi-main.label: Swollen neurone
tbi-main.title: Swollen neurone
tbi-main.body: Sheared, energy-poor neurones swell and release excitotoxic transmitters.
tbi-main.care: Helps: Head up 30 degrees; Hypertonic saline; Sedation and analgesia; CSF drainage; Evacuate a mass lesion; Keep CPP at 60 or above. Avoid: Hypotension; Hypotonic fluids; Hypoxia or hypercapnia.

status-main.label: Medial temporal lobe
status-main.title: Medial temporal lobe
status-main.body: The hippocampus and its neighbours are most vulnerable to prolonged seizures.
status-main.care: Helps: First line benzodiazepine; Second line antiseizure drug; Anaesthetic infusion in refractory status; Treat the cause; Correct glucose and electrolytes. Avoid: Delayed first treatment; Under-dosed benzodiazepine.

status-main.label: Cortical injury
status-main.title: Cortical injury
status-main.body: Congested, swollen cortex where seizure activity burned more fuel than it was given.
status-main.care: Helps: First line benzodiazepine; Second line antiseizure drug; Anaesthetic infusion in refractory status; Treat the cause; Correct glucose and electrolytes. Avoid: Delayed first treatment; Under-dosed benzodiazepine.

status-main.label: Swollen cortex
status-main.title: Swollen cortex
status-main.body: Swollen grey matter with blurred grey-white junction.
status-main.care: Helps: First line benzodiazepine; Second line antiseizure drug; Anaesthetic infusion in refractory status; Treat the cause; Correct glucose and electrolytes. Avoid: Delayed first treatment; Under-dosed benzodiazepine.

status-main.label: Excitotoxic neurone
status-main.title: Excitotoxic neurone
status-main.body: Continuous firing and calcium entry swell the neurone and exhaust its energy.
status-main.care: Helps: First line benzodiazepine; Second line antiseizure drug; Anaesthetic infusion in refractory status; Treat the cause; Correct glucose and electrolytes. Avoid: Delayed first treatment; Under-dosed benzodiazepine.

sepsis-main.label: Dilated arteriole
sepsis-main.title: Dilated arteriole
sepsis-main.body: Nitric oxide relaxes the vessel muscle, so resistance and blood pressure fall.
sepsis-main.care: Helps: Antibiotics within one hour; Source control; Balanced crystalloid; Noradrenaline; Hydrocortisone in refractory shock. Avoid: Delayed antibiotics; Large fluid overload; Starch colloid.

sepsis-main.label: Leaky endothelium
sepsis-main.title: Leaky endothelium
sepsis-main.body: The lining loses its coat and its tight junctions. Plasma leaks into the tissue.
sepsis-main.care: Helps: Antibiotics within one hour; Source control; Balanced crystalloid; Noradrenaline; Hydrocortisone in refractory shock. Avoid: Delayed antibiotics; Large fluid overload; Starch colloid.

dic-main.label: Fibrin plugs
dic-main.title: Fibrin plugs
dic-main.body: Fibrin blocks small vessels, starving the tissue behind them.
dic-main.care: Helps: Treat the underlying cause; Platelets if bleeding or very low; Plasma or cryoprecipitate if bleeding; Heparin in thrombosis predominant DIC; Natural anticoagulant replacement. Avoid: Tranexamic acid; Invasive procedures without correction.

dic-main.label: Fibrin mesh
dic-main.title: Fibrin mesh
dic-main.body: Thrombin turns fibrinogen into strands that trap red cells and platelets.
dic-main.care: Helps: Treat the underlying cause; Platelets if bleeding or very low; Plasma or cryoprecipitate if bleeding; Heparin in thrombosis predominant DIC; Natural anticoagulant replacement. Avoid: Tranexamic acid; Invasive procedures without correction.

dic-main.label: Tissue factor displayed
dic-main.title: Tissue factor
dic-main.body: Activated endothelium displays tissue factor and switches on clotting.
dic-main.care: Helps: Treat the underlying cause; Platelets if bleeding or very low; Plasma or cryoprecipitate if bleeding; Heparin in thrombosis predominant DIC; Natural anticoagulant replacement. Avoid: Tranexamic acid; Invasive procedures without correction.
